prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Scottish National Party Manifesto 2001 – Summary (ideological framing preserved)

- Scotland first, independence now: A vote for SNP MPs is a vote for Scotland, a vote for independence, and a stronger Scottish Parliament. More SNP MPs strengthens the case for a referendum; a majority of SNP MPs will trigger one. SNP MPs have no split loyalty and will oppose anti-Scottish measures at Westminster.

- Independence vision: Complete the powers of Scotland’s Parliament to build a just, caring, enterprising nation. Use Scotland’s wealth for Scotland, with normal status in the world and 21st‑century self-government.

- Investing Scotland’s wealth: Create a Scottish Fund for Future Generations by committing surplus oil revenues (e.g., £4.9bn in one year yielding £390m+ per year in perpetuity; over £1bn per year within five years). Establish a Scottish Trust for Public Investment to beat costly PFI/PPP, halving capital costs and unlocking major infrastructure investment.

- Democracy and constitution: Written constitution with inclusive citizenship; the Queen as Head of State subject to referendum; proportional representation at all levels; cut quangos and enhance parliamentary oversight; secure civil service opportunities in an independent Scotland.

- Education: Free access to higher education—abolish tuition fees and rebuild grants; moratorium on disruptive change via an Education Convention; P1–P3 class sizes to 18; end misleading league tables; major school refurbishment; statutory duty to provide Gaelic-medium education; anti-racism and inclusion.

- Jobs and enterprise: Targeted infrastructure (roads, rail, air, digital broadband nationwide); refocus enterprise agencies; elevate tourism with Scotland-led marketing and better access; devolve and improve the New Deal; raise minimum wage to £4.36 for all ages; Charter of Trade Union Rights.

- Environment and energy: National Environment Plan; oppose UK climate levy’s harm to hydro; 12% of energy and 25% of electricity from renewables by 2010; no new nuclear, decommission existing plants; back resource efficiency; reform water to halt price hikes and backdoor privatisation.

- Health and care: National Health Care Commission to end postcode treatment; HTBS decisions binding; free dental check-ups; freeze and review prescription charges; invest via STPI, add 1,500 nurses, Clean Hospitals Fund, halve waiting times; free personal care for all elderly.

- Europe: Scotland in Europe—confederal cooperation, subsidiarity, no superstate; euro only by conditions and referendum; independence brings full representation, votes and a Commissioner.

- Defence and international: Remove Trident; oppose US missile defence; negotiate phased withdrawal from NATO; build a professional Scottish Defence Force; business-focused external offices; meet UN aid targets and cancel Third World debt.

- Social justice and communities: National anti-poverty strategy and poverty-proofing; fair, fast asylum processes (end vouchers); relieve council housing debt, invest via STPI, oppose wholesale stock transfer; three‑year core funding for voluntary sector; tackle homelessness.

- Equality, disability, crime and drugs: Enshrine equal opportunities; strengthen Disability Discrimination Act; more police (+1,000); Drugs Courts; parental responsibility orders; lifelong supervision for high‑risk sex offenders.

- Tax and local government: No overall tax rise without mandate; Comprehensive Review of Taxation for fairness and simplicity; immediate 10p/gal fuel duty cut funded by a new 5p income tax band over £100k; PR for councils; review local income tax.

- Rural, agriculture, fisheries, land: Cut fuel burdens; improve rural transport and digital access; fair EU implementation timing; promote diversification and organic; reform CFP with zonal management; support processors and aquaculture; salmon-farming inquiry; empower community right‑to‑buy.

- Pensions and social security: Restore earnings link; spread winter fuel payments weekly; streamline benefits, improve take‑up; fairer disability and carers’ support.

- Transport: STPI-backed investment; Regional Transport Authorities; public share in Railtrack; reopen key lines (including Borders), electrify priority routes, airport rail links; light rail in cities; upgrade M74, A9 and other bottlenecks; cheaper ferries with RET pilots; abolish Skye Bridge tolls.
